questions.q: The principle of 'Utmost Good Faith' (Uberrima Fides) means:

options: Insured is restored to pre-loss position, no profit
questions.explanation: Indemnity = insured cannot profit from insurance. Only actual loss is compensated.

questions.q: 'Proximate Cause' (Causa Proxima) determines:
options: The dominant/effective cause of the loss
questions.explanation: The nearest, dominant cause of loss — to decide if it falls within the policy coverage.

questions.q: Which is NOT an input device?

questions.q: RAM is volatile because it:
options: Loses data when power is off
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile — data is lost when the computer shuts down.

questions.q: Which memory is non-volatile?
questions.explanation: ROM (Read Only Memory) retains data without power. EEPROM/Flash are also non-volatile.

questions.q: 1 GB equals:
BIOS stands for:
questions.explanation: BIOS: firmware that initialises hardware during boot. Now often replaced by UEFI.

questions.q: Third generation computers used:
questions.explanation: 1st: vacuum tubes, 2nd: transistors, 3rd: ICs (1964-71), 4th: microprocessors, 5th: AI/parallel.

questions.q: ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) is part of:
questions.explanation: ALU is inside the CPU — performs arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.q: An interpreter translates code:
questions.explanation: Interpreter: one line at a time. Compiler: entire program at once into machine code.

questions.q: SSD stands for:
questions.explanation: SSD uses flash memory, no moving parts — faster, more durable than HDD.

questions.q: The process of starting a computer is called:
questions.explanation: Booting: loading OS into memory. Cold boot = from off; warm boot = restart.

questions.q: Processor speed is measured in:
questions.explanation: GHz (gigahertz) = billions of clock cycles per second.

questions.q: Cache memory is used to:
options: Speed up CPU access to frequently used data
questions.explanation: Cache: small, fast memory between CPU and RAM storing frequently accessed data.

questions.q: USB stands for:
questions.explanation: USB: standard interface for connecting peripherals.

questions.q: GPU stands for:
questions.explanation: GPU: specialised processor for rendering graphics and parallel computation.

questions.q: HDMI is used to connect:
questions.explanation: HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface): transmits video + audio digitally.

questions.q: Binary number system uses base:
questions.explanation: Binary = base 2 (0,1). Octal = 8, Decimal = 10, Hexadecimal = 16.

questions.q: Which is a high-level programming language?
questions.explanation: Python is high-level. Machine (binary) and assembly are low-level.

questions.q: An operating system is an example of:
questions.explanation: OS is system software managing hardware and providing services to applications.

questions.q: ASCII stands for:
options: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
questions.explanation: ASCII: 7-bit character encoding (128 characters). Extended ASCII uses 8 bits.

questions.q: What does IoT stand for?
questions.explanation: IoT: interconnected everyday devices communicating over the internet.

questions.q: Which is NOT an operating system?
questions.explanation: Oracle is an RDBMS. Windows, Linux, macOS are operating systems.

questions.q: Linux is an example of:
questions.explanation: Linux: open-source under GPL license. Source code freely available.

questions.q: The 'kernel' of an OS is:
questions.explanation: Kernel: core of OS managing memory, processes, devices, system calls.

questions.q: Windows uses which default file system?
questions.explanation: NTFS (New Technology File System). ext4 = Linux, HFS+ = older macOS.

questions.q: Android OS is based on:
questions.explanation: Android built on Linux kernel, developed primarily by Google.

questions.q: Virtual memory uses part of which storage as extended RAM?
questions.explanation: Virtual memory: uses disk page file/swap space when physical RAM is full.

questions.q: UNIX was developed at:
questions.explanation: UNIX: 1969 at AT&T Bell Labs by Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie.

questions.q: In Windows, Ctrl+Alt+Delete opens:
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Alt+Delete: security screen. Ctrl+Shift+Esc: Task Manager directly.

questions.q: GUI stands for:
questions.explanation: GUI: windows, icons, menus, pointers. Contrast with CLI (Command Line Interface).

questions.q: Multitasking means:
questions.explanation: OS runs multiple programs concurrently by managing CPU time sharing.

questions.q: Ctrl + B in MS Word:
questions.explanation: Ctrl+B: toggle bold. Ctrl+I: italic. Ctrl+U: underline.

questions.q: Default file extension for Word 2007+ is:
questions.explanation: .docx (Office Open XML). Older format was .doc.

questions.q: =AVERAGE() in Excel calculates:
questions.explanation: =AVERAGE(range) returns the arithmetic mean. No built-in MEAN() in Excel.

questions.q: Cell address 'B5' means:
questions.explanation: Letter = column, number = row. B5 = Column B, Row 5.

questions.q: Ctrl + ; in Excel inserts:
questions.explanation: Ctrl+; = today's date. Ctrl+Shift+; = current time.

questions.q: =VLOOKUP() stands for:
questions.explanation: Searches first column of a range, returns a value from a specified column in the same row.

questions.q: '$A$1' in Excel is an example of:
questions.explanation: $A$1 = absolute (both locked). A1 = relative. $A1 or A$1 = mixed.

questions.q: Max rows in Excel 2007+ worksheet:
F5 in PowerPoint:
questions.explanation: F5: slideshow from slide 1. Shift+F5: from current slide.

questions.q: Ctrl + Z is used for:
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Z = Undo. Ctrl+Y = Redo.

questions.q: Mail Merge in Word is found under which tab?

questions.q: =COUNT() in Excel counts:

questions.q: Ctrl + N in Excel creates a:

questions.q: Print Layout view in Word shows:
questions.explanation: Print Layout: headers, footers, margins — exact printed output.

questions.q: PowerPoint file extension is:
questions.explanation: .pptx since Office 2007. Older format was .ppt.

questions.q: =IF() function in Excel is used for:
questions.explanation: =IF(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false). Most-used logical function.

questions.q: Ctrl + P is used to:
questions.explanation: Ctrl+P = Print dialog in all Office apps.

questions.q: Which function joins text from multiple cells in Excel?

questions.q: Ctrl + F is used to:
questions.explanation: Ctrl+F = Find. Ctrl+H = Find & Replace.

questions.q: In Excel, what does '#VALUE!' error mean?

questions.q: HTTP stands for:
questions.explanation: HTTP: protocol for transmitting web pages. HTTPS adds SSL/TLS encryption.

questions.q: An IP address uniquely identifies:
questions.explanation: IP (Internet Protocol) address: unique identifier for each network device.

questions.q: SMTP is used for:
questions.explanation: SMTP = Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (sending). POP3/IMAP = receiving.

questions.q: DNS translates:
questions.explanation: DNS = Domain Name System. google.com → 142.250.x.x.

questions.q: A Router connects:
options: Multiple networks and routes data packets
questions.explanation: Router: routes packets between networks using IP addresses. Switch: within a LAN.

questions.q: Star topology connects all devices to a:
questions.explanation: Star: all nodes → central hub. Bus: single cable. Ring: circular. Mesh: all-to-all.

questions.q: Phishing is:
options: Cyber fraud via fake emails/websites to steal data
questions.explanation: Social engineering attack impersonating trusted entities to steal passwords/card details.

questions.q: A Firewall protects a network by:
options: Monitoring and controlling traffic based on security rules
questions.explanation: Firewall: monitors incoming/outgoing traffic, blocks unauthorised access.

questions.q: FTP stands for:
questions.explanation: FTP: transfers files between client and server over a network.

questions.q: HTTPS provides security through:
questions.explanation: HTTPS = HTTP + SSL/TLS. Encrypts data between browser and server.

questions.q: Ransomware is malware that:
questions.explanation: Encrypts victim's files, demands ransom (often cryptocurrency) for decryption key.

questions.q: OSI model has how many layers?
questions.explanation: 7: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

questions.q: The Network layer (Layer 3) handles:
questions.explanation: Layer 3: routing, forwarding, IP addressing. Layer 4: Transport (TCP/UDP).

questions.q: VPN stands for:
questions.explanation: VPN: encrypted tunnel over public network for private, secure communication.

questions.q: URL stands for:
questions.explanation: URL = Uniform Resource Locator — the address of a web resource.

questions.q: ISP stands for:
questions.explanation: ISP: company providing internet access (Jio, Airtel, BSNL, etc.).

questions.q: LAN covers:
options: A small area like a building/campus
questions.explanation: LAN = Local Area Network. WAN = Wide Area Network (country/global). MAN = Metropolitan.

questions.q: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) uses:
questions.explanation: 2FA: e.g., password + OTP, or password + biometric. Enhances security.

questions.q: 'Cloud Computing' means:
options: Accessing data/services over the internet on demand
questions.explanation: Delivers computing services (storage, servers, databases) over the internet. Examples: AWS, Azure, GCP.

questions.q: SaaS stands for:
questions.explanation: SaaS (Gmail, Office 365). PaaS = Platform. IaaS = Infrastructure.

questions.q: SQL stands for:
questions.explanation: SQL: manages and queries relational databases.

questions.q: A Primary Key in a database:
options: Uniquely identifies each row, cannot be NULL or duplicate
questions.explanation: Primary key: unique, non-null identifier for each record in a table.

questions.q: SELECT in SQL is used to:
questions.explanation: SELECT: retrieves data. INSERT: adds. UPDATE: modifies. DELETE: removes.

questions.q: AWS stands for:
questions.explanation: AWS: largest cloud provider. Others: Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform.

questions.q: PDF stands for:
questions.explanation: PDF: developed by Adobe for device-independent document sharing.

questions.q: An Algorithm is:
options: A step-by-step procedure to solve a problem
questions.explanation: Finite, ordered set of well-defined instructions for solving a computational problem.

questions.q: Blockchain is primarily:
questions.explanation: Blockchain: immutable distributed ledger — basis of cryptocurrencies and decentralised applications.

questions.q: Mozilla Firefox is an example of:
questions.explanation: Firefox: open-source (Mozilla Public License). Chrome, Edge, Safari are proprietary.

questions.q: AI stands for:
questions.explanation: AI: machines simulating human intelligence — learning, reasoning, problem-solving.

questions.q: 'Deepfake' technology uses AI to:
options: Create realistic fake videos/images of people
questions.explanation: Deepfakes use deep learning to generate convincing fake media — a growing cybersecurity concern.
